summary: Continuation design (round 3). The earlier architecture is kept: the requirement now says start-up is proven by in-process tests, so round 2's smoke runner and its scripts/smoke scope are dropped. Cloud mode uses ASP.NET Core Identity with a Dapper/QBuilder IUserStore (no EF Core), 7-day cookie sessions, Google through the framework's AddOAuth (no new package), one fixed role per person (Admin/Operator/Viewer, no RoleManager or role table, an IUserRoleStore adapter over the single Role column plus role and company_id claims), and tenancy taken from the signed-in person's CompanyId claim, never from a header or subdomain. Desktop/local mode registers no auth and keeps its SQLite stores, so data stays intact (R11). Already in the working tree and to be kept: Modules/Identity/** (AppUser, DapperUserStore, IdentityRepository, LegacyAwarePasswordHasher, AppClaimsPrincipalFactory, RoleAccessRules and handler, AuthEndpoints, GoogleSignIn, RegistrationService, TeamEndpoints, TeamRepository, DTOs), Shared/Tenancy (ICompanyContext, CompanyScope), company-scoped Mariadb stores, migrations 0001_identity and 0002_drop_legacy_auth with MigrationRunner, settings cleanup (JWT_KEY, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD removed; GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET added; SMTP settings kept), front-end auth client, login/signup/forgot/reset/change-password pages, Team page, role-aware AppShell, and the backend and jest tests. The old stack (AuthRouter, JwtMiddleware, JwtService, TokenService, SetupService, PasswordHelper, RefreshToken and ResetToken) is already deleted. Finishing work, test-first: (1) Re-run the full backend and jest suites and the typecheck to confirm the baseline is green, and fix anything red. (2) Close the cheap in-scope hardening notes, each with a failing test first: session cookie Secure always in cloud mode (so TLS terminated at a proxy still yields a Secure cookie); rotate the security stamp on role change and password reset so old sessions and reset links die; Google link-on-match only when Google reports the email verified (tested already; record the accepted risk in SETUP.md); DataProtection keys under the directory the app resolves for SHIPRIGHT_DATA_DIR. (3) Every public endpoint (login, register, providers, forgot-password, reset-password, google start and complete) carries an AllowAnonymous reason comment and the route-sweep test lists exactly those and expects 'sign in required' (401) for all others (API-001); desktop mode satisfies this with no sign-in screen. (4) Prove BOOT-001 with in-process automated tests only: no scripts/smoke runner and no other start-up harness is created. A new test file Modules/Identity/BootInProcessTests.cs starts the app with WebApplicationFactory in desktop/local mode (SQLite in a temp data dir, no sign-in: GET /api/health, GET / and GET /api/projects succeed with no credentials, no sign-in routes exist) and in signed-in server mode against the test MariaDB named by the project's own test-database setting (GET /api/projects without credentials returns 401; after register the same read returns 200 with the session cookie). Existing CloudApiFactory and InMemoryCloudFactory are reused. Also an automated settings-agreement test compares .env.example, docker-compose.yml and CloudConfiguration exactly and fails on any difference. (5) Confirm tests exist for the non-functional checks: lockout after 5 wrong passwords for 5 minutes, sign-in and 50-person team list under 1 second, no partial company/person records when registration, Google first sign-in or teammate creation fails mid-way (company and person inserted in one transaction), and no passwords, reset links or Google tokens in logs or responses. Confirm every list endpoint stays paged (team list: default 20, max 50, ordered by name, total returned, index on CompanyId+Name) and every write returns RFC 7807 field errors. Scale and cost: no change in desktop mode; in cloud mode one primary-key read per person per minute for stamp validation, one indexed CompanyId filter per query, team list bounded to 50 rows per page, sign-in limited by the existing rate limiter and lockout, no new threads, timers, packages or startup work beyond one idempotent migration check. The boot tests cost two in-process app starts only when tests run and nothing at app runtime. The last-active-Admin rule is enforced in the same UPDATE statement to avoid races. Open items for sign-off: legacy rows without a company are assigned to the oldest company; SshKeyStore is file-based per machine and is not company-scoped by this change.
